display.purpose: The single heading on standalone screens (login, guest done screen).

shadows.name: pick-up

shadows.name: card-ring

motion.name: deck-return
motion.purpose: A released card that did not commit springs back to center.

motion.name: deck-leave
motion.purpose: A voted card flies off 150% of its width, rotated 20deg.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The deck skips the fly-off animation entirely.

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius, 8px); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font: 500 14px/1 'Inter Variable', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.css: .ds-btn-fab { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; height: 56px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: calc(var(--radius, 8px) * 1.8); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font: 700 15px/1 'Inter Variable', sans-serif; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-fab:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-fab:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-fab:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.css: .ds-votes { display: flex; gap: 24px; justify-content: center; } .ds-vote { width: 56px; height: 56px; border-radius: 9999px; display: grid; place-items: center; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-vote-no { background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); border: 1px solid var(--border); } .ds-vote-no:hover { background: var(--muted); } .ds-vote-yes { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); border: 0; } .ds-vote-yes:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 80%, transparent); } .ds-vote:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring) 50%, transparent); } .ds-vote:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

narrative.overview:
Lumia is a photographer's light table. The surface is even, neutral and quiet, and the only things that glow on it are the photos and the one action that matters on each screen. The interface steps back: no tinted backgrounds, no decorative color, no ornament that competes with a picture. Warmth lives in a single place, the toasted-honey accent, and it is spent sparingly.

Every surface is a task surface (Operate mode). The owner manages albums and reads results; the guest swipes through a deck. Both happen on a phone first, inside a single centered column, so density stays moderate and touch targets stay generous. The components are tactile and friendly: soft corners, a physical response to touch (the deck card follows the finger and tilts, buttons dip a pixel on press), and large round voting buttons a thumb can find without looking.

Light and dark are equal citizens. The app follows the system preference, with no theme switch, and every token has a pair. In dark mode the table becomes a graphite viewer and the honey lightens so it still reads as the one source of light.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral graphite surfaces with zero chroma; the honey accent is the only hue in the chrome.
Photos carry the color and get the space.
One centered column (448px max) on every screen, phone-first.
Flat at rest; shadows only on things you can pick up (deck cards, the floating upload button).
Tactile, soft-cornered controls with physical feedback.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Honey is the only hue in the interface. If a screen has two honey elements competing, one of them is wrong. Photos are the only other color allowed.

rules.name: The Honey Means Yes Rule
rules.body: A positive vote is honey, a negative vote is ember, everywhere: in the deck, the viewer's selected state and the small vote marks on thumbnails. Never green.

rules.name: The Neutral Selection Rule
rules.body: The selected option of a selector (filters, groupings, sort, tabs) is graphite: the button `selected` variant, or a foreground underline for tabs. Selection is state, not an action, so it never takes honey.

rules.name: The Paired Token Rule
rules.body: Never write a raw color in a component. Every color is a token with a light and a dark value, so dark mode cannot drift.

rules.name: The Readable Signal Rule
rules.body: Any token used as text (foreground, pencil, honey, ember) must reach 4.5:1 on both the page and the tray, in light and in dark. Check a new value before shipping it.

rules.name: The Weight Not Face Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is a heavier weight of Inter, never a new font, italic or color.

rules.name: The Pick-Up Rule
rules.body: If you can't drag it or it doesn't float over content, it doesn't get a shadow.

dos: Do let photos take the space: full-bleed in the deck, square `object-cover` tiles in grids.
Do use honey for exactly one primary action per screen, plus positive-vote signals and the active-link dot.
Do define every new color as a light/dark token pair in `styles.css`.
Do keep everything inside the 448px column with 16px side padding.

Do keep every touch target at 44px or more: the default button, icon button and input are 44px. The `sm` (36px) and `icon-sm` sizes are only for secondary controls laid over photos, such as the delete button on an owner's thumbnail.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any movement beyond a color change.
donts: Don't tint backgrounds or cards; the table is neutral.
Don't use green for "me gusta", or honey for a selected option, a tab or a brand mark.
Don't stack an icon tile above a heading.
Don't add shadows to cards, lists or dialogs at rest (The Pick-Up Rule).
Don't add a second typeface or use color for emphasis in text.
Don't use solid red fills; destructive actions are an ember tint.
Don't add a theme switch; the app follows the system preference.
